In this case, the treated doctor has not been examined regarding the disability suffered by the claimant.
The Tribunal has therefore not awarded any compensation towards loss of future income.

3. The Tribunal has noticed that the claimant himself admitted that there had been no loss of income as a result of the accident and therefore, disentitling him of the compensation towards future loss of income cannot be found fault with.
4. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards pain and suffering and a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards loss of amenities in life, apart from a sum of Rs.5,62,524/- towards medical expenses.
In my view, these awards are just and proper and do not require any enhancement.
5. The evidence on record also indicates that the claimant was hospitalised for nearly three months.

In my view, in the light of the length of hospitalisation, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- towards food, nourishment, conveyance, attendant charges and other incidental charges.
6. The Tribunal has not awarded any compensation towards loss of income during laid up period.

Having regard to the length of hospitalisation, it would be appropriate to determine the laid up period as five months and award a sum of Rs.45,000/- towards the loss of income during laid up period, as the monthly notional income of the claimant is determined at Rs.9,000/- as per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accidents of the year 2015.

7. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant would be entitled to the following compensation:
